rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative particle لا foretells that God will keep Muhammad steadfast on the straight path and that the opponents will not attain it, a prophetic sign.
rows.anchor: لا يكاد يتحقق حتى يمضي زمن فيصير مستقبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما belittles every object worshipped besides God, including inanimate idols, and covers worship now and in the future, privately or publicly.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في معبوداتهم ما لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with disavowal of shirk purifies falsehood before addressing other duties; worship mixed with association is invalid.
rows.anchor: ولما بدأ بما هو الأحق بالبداءة وهو البراءة من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the opponents worship God in association with idols, the nominal clause denies a stable, creditable worship; a verbal clause would deny every small or great instance.
rows.anchor: نفى عبادتهم له في الجملة الاسمية الدالة على الثبات لا في الفعلية الدالة على نفي كل قليل وكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ما for the object of Muhammad's worship is fair because it can refer to God and the opponents acknowledge that his object is knowing; God is too remote from them for agreement.
rows.anchor: وكانت ( ما ) صالحة للإطلاق عليه سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad had never worshipped their objects, even before prophethood; Arabs also improvised arbitrary roadside gods from stones or earth mixed with milk.
rows.anchor: وكانوا غير مقتصرين على عبادة أصنامهم التي اتخذوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated denial extends to the present and future, correcting any inference that only current worship was denied and confirming Muhammad's complete separation from them.
rows.anchor: نفى ذلك في الاستقبال أيضا علما من أعلام النبوة مع تأكيد ما أفادته الجملة الماضية

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: A present-tense verb may denote an occurrence without a specified time, so the wording can include Muhammad's past worship of God as well as present and future worship.
rows.anchor: ذكر أبو حيان وغيره في سورة الحج عند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents' religion has no sound foundation or evidence, and they persist in it to death; the verse predicts that some will die naturally and others by Muhammad's sword.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تعلمون أنه لا أصل له يثبت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's religion is Islam, from its garden to certainty and spiritual excellence; its evidence is clear, while the opponents cannot share it or turn him from it.
rows.anchor: من واصع روضة الإسلام إلى أعلى مقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophecy is fulfilled because many opponents remained unbelievers and God completed Muhammad's religion; later converts were not the entrenched unbelievers meant here.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه علما من أعلام النبوة نم حيث إنه مات منهم ناس كثير بعد ذلك على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses need no emphasis because their meaning is completely clear; the final exclusive assignment of religions circles back to the opening denial of worship.
rows.anchor: وساق الجمل كلها غير مؤكد إشارة إلى أنها من الوضوح في حد لا خفاء به أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah grants no permission to disbelieve and imposes no bar to jihad, so there is no abrogation to explain.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه إذن في الكفر ولا منع عن الجهاد ليحتاج إلى نسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's concise, miraculous argument cuts off every hope that Muhammad would ever associate another with God; it corresponds to al-Anam, the sixth surah from the beginning, as this is sixth from the end.
rows.anchor: من أعظم الدلائل إعجازها وجمعها للمعاني في إشارتها وإيجازها أن حاصلها قطع رجاء أهل الكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's wording links to al-Anam's declarations that God alone is taken as protector, judge, and Lord.
rows.anchor: أغير الله أبغي ربا وهو رب كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai's word arithmetic counts twenty-seven written words, thirty-one with the basmala, then forty-four including hidden and explicit pronouns; thirteen hidden pronouns evoke Muhammad's concealed thirteen-year Meccan residence.
rows.anchor: وكلماتها الخطية سبع وعشرون إلى أربع كلمات البسملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thirty-one non-pronoun words are associated with Yazdegerd's death in year 31; matching al-Kawthar's letter count signifies few followers surpassing many enemies.
rows.anchor: وغير الضمائر إحدى وثلاثون المناظر لها من السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, ten thousand Muslims faced the Quraysh and their allies, whom the source says were beyond counting.
rows.anchor: من قريش ومن حولهم لا يحصون كثرة

rows.speaker: حماس
rows.claim: A fleeing opponent's poem recalls Safwan and Ikrima fleeing at Khandaq and Muslims striking with swords, illustrating the defeat of the Quraysh at Mecca.
rows.anchor: اعتذار حماس الذي كان يعد امرأته أن يخدمها بعض المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Trench, ten thousand polytheists surrounded Muslims who lacked a quarter of their number and outside aid; God's support sustained them.
rows.anchor: والمشركون في عشرة آلاف وهم لا يبلغون ربعهم ولا مدد لهم ممن حولهم ولا ناصر إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written and pronounced forms of victory match the written word count of al-Kafirun, symbolizing that even weak Muslims can withstand the strongest unbelievers by God's aid.
rows.anchor: بلوغ عدد كلمات النصر خطيها واصطلاحيها ظاهرها ومستترها إلى عدد كلمات الكافرون الخطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah, also called al-Tawdi (Farewell), announces completion of religion, which entails Muhammad's death and shows that his mission was to exalt God's word and defeat Satan's.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الإعلام بتمام الدين اللازم عن مدلول اسمها النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's names and its revelation during the days of Tashriq in the Farewell Pilgrimage also signal Muhammad's unique role as the greatest servant of God.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك أيضا دل اسمها التوديع وحال نزولها وهو أيام التشريق من سنة حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala portrays God as sovereign and wise, the Merciful who sent Muhammad as mercy to all and made the Quran a clear path for worldly and afterlife welfare, and the Compassionate who guides chosen people to nearness.
rows.anchor: فعمهم بعد نعمة الإيجاد بأن بين لهم إقامة لمعاشهم ومعادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah, also named al-Tawdi, announces completed religion and thereby the Prophet's death; his mission was to exalt God and defeat Satan, and he is the greatest servant of the Beloved.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الإعلام بتمام الدين اللازم عن مدلول اسمها النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its name al-Tawdi and revelation during the Tashriq days of the Farewell Pilgrimage point to Muhammad's approaching farewell.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك أيضا دل اسمها التوديع وحال نزولها وهو أيام التشريق من سنة حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God sovereign and wise, describes Muhammad's message as mercy and the Quran as guidance for worldly and afterlife welfare, and says God draws chosen people into nearness.
rows.anchor: فعمهم بعد نعمة الإيجاد بأن بين لهم إقامة لمعاشهم ومعادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding surah showed unbelievers powerless under truce, this one answers whether combat will bring victory by promising believers triumph and warning unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فأجاب بهذه السورة بشارة للمؤمنين ونذارة للكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Mecca fell two years earlier, the victory was fully established only at the Farewell Pilgrimage; the surah was therefore revealed then, before the return from Hunayn.
rows.anchor: لم يكن هذا بالفعل إلا عام حجة الوداع بعد فتح مكة بسنتين كان كأنه لم يستقر الفتح إلا حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise proves God aids the wronged and raises His religion, delaying punishment without neglect; this encourages entrusting matters to Him.
rows.anchor: تحقيقا لأنه ينصر المظلوم ويعلي دينه ويمهل ولا يهمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The element governed by tasbih is brought forward to hasten the glad tidings.
rows.anchor: مقدما معمول ( سبح ) تعجيلا للبشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idha treats decrees as approaching their appointed times; majazically, coming means occurring at the divinely fixed time, even if people think it has passed.
rows.anchor: يسوقها إليها سائق القدرة , فتقرب منها شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing victory to God's supreme name magnifies it; al-fath denotes the highest, unrestricted victory, especially the conquest of Mecca promised at Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: إلى الاسم الأعظم إلى أن المراد أعلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defeat of the people of the Sanctuary humbled the Arabs; seeing God's protection of Mecca, they submitted, preparing later conquests.
rows.anchor: لا طاقة لنا بمن أظفره الله بأهل الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional style implies victory over all nations; idha marks certainty, nearness, and God's power over hearts, so the Prophet should await its arrival and prepare to thank God.
rows.anchor: بأنه لايخلف الوعد ولا ينقص ما قدره

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that once religion and law were complete and Muhammad had fulfilled his mission, he recognized that his life was ending; mass entry into Islam after hesitation was the sign.
rows.anchor: الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما كمل دينه واتضحت شريعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands frequent prescribed seeking of forgiveness after gatherings, at day's edges, and when tasks end, to cover lapses or slackness and preserve servants' time and states for their promised reward.
rows.anchor: وأمر بالإكثار من الاستغفار المشروع في أعقاب المجالس وفي أطراف النهار وخواتم المآخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's exhortation to ask forgiveness also reveals that Abu Bakr understood Muhammad's death to be near.
rows.anchor: وأن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه عرف منها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نعيت إليه نفسه الكريمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised divine words cannot be changed; the surah points to the completion announced in al-Maida 3.
rows.anchor: وتمت كلمات ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although al-Maida, Bara'a, and the Farewell Pilgrimage suggested an ending, the Companions did not identify it with certainty before this surah; they continued hoping for Muhammad's life.
rows.anchor: لكن لم يبلغنا استشعار أحد من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم تعيين الأمر إلا من هذه السورة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr became certain that the surah announced Muhammad's approaching death and wept when the Prophet recited it.
rows.anchor: استيقن أبو بكر رضي الله عنه ذلك استيقانا حمله على البكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are the Arabs, formerly held insignificant by other nations, who become the central people through Islam while the rest become their followers and subjects.
rows.anchor: أي العرب الذين كانوا حقيرين عند جميع الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their continuing entry into God's religion means entering His law and recompense, as the Arabs had denied the resurrection on which full requital depends.
rows.anchor: وعبر عنه بالدين الذين معناه الجزاء لأن العرب كانوا لا يعتقدون القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afwajan means large successive tribes and groups, including Mecca, Taif, Hawazin, and Hamdan, entering rapidly and peacefully after earlier individual conversions.
rows.anchor: أي قبائل قبائل وزمرا زمرا وجماعات كثيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs reasoned that no one could resist a man who defeated Mecca despite God's former protection of it from the people of the Elephant; the Elephant story thus foreshadowed prophethood and founded the call.
rows.anchor: ليس لنا بهم يدان . فتبين أن هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had in effect praised Himself by removing shirk from Arabia; Muhammad is to glorify Him in speech, action, prayer, and every kind of worship, in wonder and gratitude for the unexpected conquest and completed mission.
rows.anchor: أي نزه أنت بقولك وفعلك بالصلاة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek forgiveness acknowledges that no creature can fulfill God's due, and that He may forgive even grave sins; it encourages prompt repentance, good works, and hope.
rows.anchor: أي اطلب غفرانه إنه كان غفارا إيذانا بأنه لا يقدر أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istighfar after prayer, the greatest act of worship, models constant supplication and provides a second safeguard for the community as Muhammad's presence, its first safeguard, nears its end.
rows.anchor: الاستغفار عقب الصلاة التي هي أعظم العبادات لتقتدي بك أمتك في المواظبة على الأمان الثاني لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad entered Mecca bowed so low he nearly touched his saddle, showing that victory came by God's power rather than numbers; at Hunayn, victory followed an initial rout with fewer than thirty steadfast companions.
rows.anchor: دخل يوم الفتح مكة مطأطئا رأسه حتى إنه ليكاد يمس واسطة الرحل تواضعا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih signals completion of religion and fulfillment of God's promise; istighfar signals the nearing end of Muhammad's greatest worship and serves as a humble close to deeds and gatherings.
rows.anchor: التسبيح الذي هو تنزيه عن النقص إشارة إلى إكماله الدين تحقيقا لما كان تقدم به وعده الشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied command is to repent; the divine assurance addresses doubts about apostasy and emphasizes God's enduring willingness to accept a returning sinner despite His majesty.
rows.anchor: فأرشد السياق إلى أن التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly turns former unbelievers into supporters, brings them into Islam ever faster, restores the Prophet to greater honor, and returns Muslims from apostasy or sin to goodness.
rows.anchor: أي رجاعا بمن هذب به الشيطان من أهل رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the opening: God's acceptance follows the servant's repentance and istighfar, which grow from belief in divine perfection; the surah was revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage after al-Maida 3 on Arafat.
rows.anchor: فقد رجع آخر السورة إلى أولها لأنه لولا تحقق وصفه بالتوبة لما وجد الناصر الذي وجد به الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly perfection is followed by decline; on the Farewell Pilgrimage Muhammad taught the faith, made the people and God witness that he conveyed it, and said he might not meet them again the next year.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حجة الوداع وخطب الناس فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah also anticipates later apostasy and the return of some to their former faith; those irredeemably hostile are described in al-Anfal 23.
rows.anchor: ورجوع من ارتد إلى أحسن ما كانوا عليه من اعتقادهم في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abbas, or in another report his son Abd Allah, wept; Muhammad said the surah announced his death, and Abbas agreed. Umar likewise wept at al-Maida 3.
rows.anchor: بكى العباس رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah announces the religion's completion, the Last Prophet's approaching death, and victory over tyrants; these aims parallel al-Maida and connect to al-Anam 3 and al-Maida 56, 120.
rows.anchor: أن حاصلها الإيذان بكمال الدين ودنو الوفاة لخاتم النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has nineteen words, linked to year 19 AH: Caesar died while preparing to fight after Amr ibn al-As took Alexandria, sparing Muslims; Muslim victories at Caesarea, Jalula, and Istakhr further weakened Rome and Persia.
rows.anchor: وقد كان في سنة تسع عشرة من الهجرة موت قيصر

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: A report from Safina, the Prophet's freedman, says prophetic caliphate lasts thirty years before God grants kingship to whomever He wills; the author uses it to read the surah's counts as ending the caliphate.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما رواه أبو داود والترمذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting the basmala yields twenty-three words, pointing to Umar's death in 23 AH; adding eight explicit and hidden pronouns gives thirty-one, the year Hasan ended the caliphate thirty years after Muhammad's death.
rows.anchor: إذا عددت كلماتها مع البسملة كانت باعتبار الرسم ثلاثا وعشرين كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eight pronouns alone point to Mecca's conquest in year 8; explicit and implicit pronouns then encode events from years 1 through 8, including Badr, Uhud, Banu Nadir, the Confederates, Hudaybiyya, and Khaybar.
rows.anchor: وإن أخذت الضمائر وحدها بارزها ومستترها دلت على فتح مكة المشرفة بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in wa-astaghfirhu is linked to Hudaybiyya in year 6, which the Prophet called a victory; the ensuing surah and embassy to rulers were further signs of prophecy.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في السادسة عمرة الحديبية التي سماها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فتحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concealed pronoun in kana signifies the greater conquest of Mecca through the hidden divine realm, while its possible overt form also carries its own numerical sign.
rows.anchor: فلذلك كان ضمير الاستتار دالا على الفتح الأكبر بالانتصار على السكان والديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah decisively declares that even the closest unbeliever to a great victor will lose; this demonstrates the Lawgiver's unmatched sovereignty and urges all servants to affirm divine unity.
rows.anchor: مقصودها البت والقطع الحتم بخسران الكافر ولو كان أقرب الخلق إلى أعظم الفائزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following al-Ikhlas, which is associated with promised victory and many helpers, the name Tabbat plainly signals this theme.
rows.anchor: المقرون بضمان النصر وكثرة الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala names God as the Compeller and Majestic, who misguides and guides; the Merciful gives communication to friend and foe, while the Compassionate singles out the beloved for guidance.
rows.anchor: الذي عم الولي والعدو بنعمة البيان بعد الإكرام بالإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah declares certain loss even for an unbeliever related to a victorious Prophet, showing God's unmatched sovereignty and calling all servants to monotheism.
rows.anchor: مقصودها البت والقطع الحتم بخسران الكافر ولو كان أقرب الخلق إلى أعظم الفائزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement after al-Ikhlas, associated with guaranteed victory and abundant supporters, and its name Tabbat signal its theme.
rows.anchor: المقرون بضمان النصر وكثرة الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names in the basmala express majesty and guidance, universal communication to allies and enemies, and special guidance for those He favors.
rows.anchor: الذي عم الولي والعدو بنعمة البيان بعد الإكرام بالإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After announcing victory and growing Muslim numbers, the preceding surah's closing name al-Tawwab prompts the question whether notorious Abu Lahab, Muhammad's close relative and fierce enemy, would change; this surah announces his ruin.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو لهب - من ضدة العناد لهذا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the nearest relative shows that neither kinship nor alliances saved the Quraysh; the claim fulfills al-Imran 12 and reminds Muhammad of the enemies' former power.
rows.anchor: لا فرق في تكذيبه لهم بين القريب والبعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbat in the past tense presents Abu Lahab's loss as already decreed, absolute, and inescapable, ending in ruin because only the afterlife brings salvation.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن الأمر قد قضى بذلك وفرغ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike neighboring surahs, this one speaks directly in God's voice without qul, which is more decorous toward kin, strengthens divine defense of the Prophet, and intensifies the warning.
rows.anchor: عن الله ولم يفتتحها ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands signify human power, so both ruined hands imply total helplessness; the dual can also stand for the whole self, and the kunya Abu Lahab ironically matches his appearance and fate.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت اليد محل قدرة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's handsome face and wealth did not help: God judges hearts and deeds, as a Prophetic report says; his familiar kunya is clearer and avoids calling him Abd al-Uzza, since worship belongs only to the worthy.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم ولا أموالكم ولكن ينظر إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads this surah with its predecessors as announcing that Muhammad completed his mission and that even his closest enemy faces ruin; al-Kafirun separates allies from enemies and is called the purifier from hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : هذه السورة وإن نزلت على سبب خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson is that only faith protects anyone from Hell; blood relations are useless without faith.
rows.anchor: وليعلم كفار قريش وغيرهم أنه لا اعتصام لأحد من النار إلا بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus 41 and al-Tawba 71 illustrate the separation of unbelievers from the Prophet and the mutual alliance of believing men and women.
rows.anchor: أنتم بريئون ما أعمل وأنا برئ مما تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second tabbat clarifies that Abu Lahab himself, not merely his hands, perished; the first is apparently a curse and the second a factual report.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأول دعاء والثاني خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship with the righteous is not enough without following their deeds; Abu Lahab was Muhammad's uncle.
rows.anchor: لأنه عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن مكتوم
rows.claim: Ibn Maktum's lexicon treats tab and tabab as loss, ruin, or destruction, with tabban used as a curse and tabiban as an emphatic form; these meanings revolve around being cut off from good.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مكتوم في الجمع بين المحكم والعباب : التب والتباب

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd distinguishes tab as a verbal noun and tabab as a noun, while the source's other cited lexicographers connect the forms with ruin, loss, and destruction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن دريد : وكأن التب المصدر والتباب الاسم

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz explains tab as a source meaning loss, like saying 'ruin to him'; the author surveys further forms whose senses all involve loss or severance.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد الله القزاز : كأنك قلت : خسرانا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root tab and its reversal bat both center on cutting, often cutting off salvation; the added sīn in istatabba suggests attainment or completion and can distinguish a form from its analogues.
rows.anchor: والذي يحقق معاني التب ويظهر أنه يؤول

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says qada al-battata is an emphatic verbal noun used only with the definite article; the dictionary surveys batt, oath, judgment, and related forms as kinds of decisive cutting.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه : وقالوا : قعد البتة

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz gives two derivations for yabit: from abatta or from batta; both mean to cut, and the source calls both eloquent forms.
rows.anchor: قال القزاز : يبت من أبت , ويبت من بت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says fasting is invalid without resolving it at night; this may derive from ibat, to establish an obligation, or bat, to decisively impose it, both accepted as eloquent, while a further reading derives it from spending the night.
rows.anchor: ( لا صيام لمن لم يبت الصيام من الليل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon continues the cutting theme: household provisions meet a need, a single-strand rope is easy to cut, and anbata can mean becoming severed or estranged.
rows.anchor: والبتات أي بالتخفيف : متاع البيت والزاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghna means to suffice, benefit, or avert harm; the verse asks rhetorically what Abu Lahab's wealth and acquired advantages did for him, since worldly circumstances cannot save.
rows.anchor: ما أغنى } أي أجزى وناب وسد { عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasab is broader than money and includes status and useful gains produced by one's effort; none helps unless God commands it.
rows.anchor: وكان المال قد تكسب منافع هي أعظم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab used his influence and clan to oppose and discredit Muhammad in public, although he had once called him the truthful and trustworthy one.
rows.anchor: مع أنه كان قبل ذلك يناديه بالصادق الأمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abu Lahab's son Utbah harmed Muhammad, the Prophet prayed for a beast to attack him; Abu Lahab tried to protect him on a Syrian journey, but a lion found and killed him.
rows.anchor: حتى قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم سلط عيله كلبا من كلابك )

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi, a servant of al-Abbas, reports that while the secretly Muslim household heard Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith describe white angels on piebald horses at Badr, Abu Rafi identified them and Abu Lahab struck him; Umm al-Fadl wounded Abu Lahab with a tent pole.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab died six or seven nights later of al-adasa, a usually fatal pustule resembling plague; Arabs feared it and left his corpse unburied until it stank, then buried it from a distance.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما عاش إلا سبع ليال أو ستا حتى رماه الله بالعدسة فقتله

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz defines adasa as a pustule and says the verb عدس الرجل means that a man contracted it, paralleling طعن for being struck by plague.
rows.anchor: قال القزاز : كانت تعدي في الجاهلية قلما يسلم منها أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disgraceful death and burial show that nothing Abu Lahab believed could save him, an early fulfillment of the verses' prediction.
rows.anchor: من أول إعجاز هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will soon enter an enveloping fire by a promise that cannot fail; its enduring flame punishes him as he scorched the believers.
rows.anchor: { سيصلى } أي عن قرب بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhat lahab depicts fire whose companionship never ceases or goes out.
rows.anchor: أي لا تسكن ولا تخمد أبدا لأن ذلك مدلول الصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah does not prove that Abu Lahab was incapable of believing: he could have entered the fire for sin, so it gives no proof of impossible moral responsibility; only his death as an unbeliever fulfilled the prediction.
rows.anchor: وليس في السورة دليل قاطع على أنه لا يؤمن لجواز أن يكون الصلي على الفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai also reads word and pronoun counts as signs: fifteen words point to Abu Lahab's death in the fifteenth prophetic year; added basmala and pronouns are linked to the conquests and years 6, 8, 9, and 11 AH.
rows.anchor: الكلمات المتعلقة به في هذه السورة خمس عشرة كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's twenty-three words evoke the Farewell Pilgrimage, when religion was completed and Satan despaired of being worshipped in Arabia, making Abu Lahab's defeat plain to all.
rows.anchor: وعدد كلمات السورة ثلاث وعشرون وهي توازي سنة حجة الوداع سنة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife is named after the complete loss because dishonoring a man's household is especially painful to Arabs; bad company also corrupts even good nature, and pleasing people against God brings ruin.
rows.anchor: وكان أشق ما على الإنسان هتك ما يصونه من حريمه حتى أنه يبذل نفسه دون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife is Umm Jamil, sister of Abu Sufyan from the Umayya line; like her husband she will burn and lose, with no rescue from wealth, status, or lineage.
rows.anchor: أم جميل أخت أبي سفيان بن حرب أمية بن عبد شمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text avoids her kunya because her ugliness contradicts it; this supports disliking honorific titles such as Nasir al-Din when their bearers lack the qualities named.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن ذكرها بكنيتها لأن صفتها القباحة وهي ضد كنيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hammalat al-hatab means she bears Hell's fuel through slander and tale-bearing that inflamed hostility toward Muhammad; the poet's wet firewood image denotes gossip.
rows.anchor: من البيض لم تصطد على ظهر لأمة ولم تمش بين الحي بالحطب الرطب أراد النميمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wood metaphor reflects gossip's power to ignite conflict and divide people; she also carried thorns and scattered them on Muhammad's path at night.
rows.anchor: وشبهت النميمة بالحطب لأنها توقد الشر فتفرق بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim's accusative reading of hammalata treats the phrase as an insult; the following clause presents a rope around her neck, degrading her like a firewood carrier.
rows.anchor: وقراءة عاصم بالنصب للقطع على الشتم تؤدي أن امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jid means neck; masad is palm fiber or anything tightly twisted, making the rope image a picture of humiliation.
rows.anchor: أي ليف أو ليف المقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the beginning: Abu Lahab cut off kinship, strayed, tried to mislead others, abused the merciful Prophet, relied on wealth, and ruined his wife and followers; this contrasts with al-Nisa's call to kinship, kindness, and justice.
rows.anchor: وحاصل هذه السورة أن أبا لهب قطع رحمه وجار عن قصد السبيل واجتهد بعد ضلاله في إضلال غيره
